title: Golden Cheese Doughnut Rings
desc: Soft cheese doughnuts with a light sugar coating.
ingredients: Plain flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Press cheese through a sieve. Beat with sugar, vanilla sugar and yolks. Mix baking soda into sour cream, then stir into the cheese with optional vodka.
Work in flour to make a soft dough. Knead gently for about a minute on a floured surface. Roll to 1.5 cm thick; cut 6–8 cm circles and remove their centres.
Heat frying oil to 180°C. Fry in small batches for about 1 minute per side until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels and dust with icing sugar.

title: Overnight Vanilla Braided Loaves
desc: Butter-rich braided bread with a tender crumb and optional seeds.
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm water. Whisk in yolks and both sugars, then mix in flour, butter and salt for 2 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and mix 4 minutes more.
Knead on a floured surface for 1–2 minutes until soft. Place in a lightly greased bowl, cover and refrigerate overnight.

Divide into loaf portions, then split each into five ropes about 25 cm long. Pinch their tops together. Numbering strands left to right each time, cross strand 1 over 3, then 2 over 3, then 5 over 2; repeat and seal the ends.
Place on a lined tray. Beat egg with glaze water and brush over loaves. Proof 1 hour, brush again and add optional seeds. Proof another 30–60 minutes.
Bake at 175°C for 30–40 minutes until browned and hollow-sounding underneath. Cool on a rack.

title: Caraway Hearth Rye Loaf
desc: A crusty rye and wheat loaf made with an established active starter.
steps: Mix active starter with water and both flours until fully moistened. Cover and rest for 1 hour. This recipe starts with an established, bubbly rye starter.
Add salt and optional caraway. Stretch and fold gently for 10–15 minutes. Cover and ferment for 3–5 hours, until airy and roughly one-third to one-half larger.
Shape into a loaf and place seam-up in a floured proofing basket. Proof at room temperature for 1–2 hours, or refrigerate 6–10 hours and then stand out for 30–60 minutes.
Heat the oven and a lidded Dutch oven to 240°C. Turn the dough onto parchment, score and transfer carefully to the hot pot. Bake covered for 30 minutes and uncovered for 20 minutes.
The loaf should be deeply browned, with an internal temperature of 96–98°C. Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Onion and Poppy Seed Flatbreads
desc: Soft flatbreads topped with golden onions and poppy seeds.
steps: Combine flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add water and dough oil, mix and knead for about 10 minutes until elastic. Cover in a greased bowl and rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Meanwhile, finely chop onions and cook slowly in the topping oil for 15–20 minutes until golden. Season.
Divide dough into flatbread portions and flatten to about 6 mm thick on a lined tray. Spread with onions and scatter with poppy seeds.
Bake at 200°C for 15–20 minutes until the edges are golden and the centres cooked. Cool briefly before serving.

title: Soft Mash Potato Loaf
desc: Mashed potato keeps this everyday loaf moist and tender.
ingredients: Water and salt, for boiling potatoes
steps: Cube potatoes and boil in salted water until tender. Drain, mash smoothly and cool until lukewarm.
Combine warm water, yeast and sugar; leave 5–10 minutes until foamy. Mix with mash, flour, salt and oil. Knead about 10 minutes until elastic.
Cover in a greased bowl and rise for 1–1½ hours until doubled. Deflate, shape into a loaf and place in a greased loaf tin. Proof another 30–45 minutes.
Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding underneath. Cool on a rack.

title: Quick Buttermilk Griddle Rounds
desc: Small soda breads cooked in a pan, with no yeast or proofing.
steps: Mix flour, soda and salt. Gradually stir in buttermilk to form a soft dough. Knead gently on a floured surface for 1–2 minutes.
Roll to about 1.3 cm thick and cut into rounds. Lightly grease a pan and heat over medium heat.
Cook rounds for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and cooked in the centre. Serve warm. Alternatively bake at 190°C for 10–12 minutes.

title: Cabbage and Mushroom Pastry Bites
desc: Small yeast pastries filled with sauerkraut and mushrooms.
steps: If starting with dried mushrooms, soak overnight in the fridge, drain and chop; measure after soaking. Reserve the strained soaking liquid.
Use one-third of the dough milk and a little of the measured flour to activate yeast with its sugar for 15 minutes. Add remaining dough ingredients and knead 10 minutes. Cover and rise 1 hour.

Simmer sauerkraut with measured mushroom liquid, bay, allspice and filling sugar for 1 hour; drain and discard whole spices. Fry chopped onion in oil until golden, add mushrooms for 5 minutes, then cabbage for 15–20 minutes until fairly dry. Season and cool.
Roll dough into a rectangle about 30 × 48 cm for the base batch and cut into four strips. Put filling along each centre, seal into logs and cut into bite-sized rolls.
Place seam-down on a lined tray. Proof 20 minutes. Brush with yolk mixed with glaze milk, add optional sesame and bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes.
ferment: 1 hr 35 min; overnight mushroom soak if needed

title: Pillowy Milk Steamed Buns
desc: Soft enriched buns steamed until light and fluffy.
steps: Stir yeast, sugar, yeast-mixture flour and its milk together. Cover and leave 15–20 minutes until bubbly.
Add the remaining flour, milk, eggs, butter and salt. Knead for 5–7 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover in a greased bowl and rise about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into bun portions and shape into balls. Cover on a floured surface and proof for 15 minutes.
Bring steamer water to a boil. Arrange buns with room to expand above the water, cover and steam for about 15 minutes until cooked through. Work in batches as needed.

title: Orange Orchard Fruit Loaf
desc: A butter cake with dried fruit, almonds and a citrus glaze.
steps: Heat oven to 190°C and line an 11 × 25 cm loaf tin. Finely chop dried fruit and almonds.
Beat butter and cake icing sugar until fluffy, about 7 minutes. Beat in yolks one at a time until pale. Separately whisk whites and salt to stiff peaks.
Combine flour, vanilla sugar, baking powder, fruit, nuts and zest. Fold into the butter mixture alternately with milk, then gently fold in whites in three additions.
Fill the tin and bake 40–45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool slightly.
Warm the citrus juice, remove from heat and whisk in glaze sugar. Drizzle over the loaf.

title: Seeded Twisted Bread Rings
desc: Chewy bread rings briefly boiled before baking with a seed topping.
steps: Mix warm water, milk, sugar and yeast. Leave about 20 minutes until frothy. Add flour, dough salt and butter; knead until smooth.
Cover and rest 15–25 minutes. Divide into ring portions. Roll each into a rope about 20 cm long, twist and firmly join the ends.
Bring a wide pot of water to a boil with the boiling salt. Simmer rings in batches for 1 minute, then lift onto lined trays.
Brush with beaten egg and scatter with seeds. Bake at 200°C for about 20 minutes until risen and golden.

title: Golden Mushroom Baguette Melts
desc: Toasted baguette loaded with mushrooms, melted cheese and herbs.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C. Cut the baguette crosswise, then split each piece lengthwise to make open-faced portions.
Finely chop onion and mushrooms. Soften onion in half the butter for about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and more butter as needed; cook about 5 minutes until their moisture evaporates. Season.
Top bread with the mushroom mixture and grated cheese. Bake for 7–10 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned.
Finish with ketchup, chopped herbs and optional crispy onions. Serve hot.
